questions.q: What column is used as the shared join key between the two extracts?
options: SalesOrderID
CustomerID
TerritoryID
LineTotal
questions.explain: SalesOrderID is the one reliable column both cleaned extracts share.

questions.q: What does how="left" do in pd.merge(customer_df, territory_df[...], on="SalesOrderID", how="left")?
options: Keeps every row from customer_df, filling unmatched territory columns with NaN
Keeps only rows that match in both DataFrames
Keeps every row from territory_df instead
Deletes any row with a missing value
questions.explain: A left join preserves all rows from the left DataFrame (customer_df), which matters so the segment analysis doesn't lose rows.

questions.q: Why does this project use how="left" instead of an inner join here?
options: The Marketing Manager's segment analysis shouldn't silently lose customer rows just because a handful of orders are missing from the territory extract
Inner joins are not supported by pandas
Left joins run faster than inner joins in all cases
TerritoryName cannot be used in an inner join
questions.explain: An inner join would drop unmatched rows, shrinking the customer segment totals -- the left join avoids that.

questions.q: What happens to rows where SalesOrderID has no match in the territory extract after the merge?
options: They are filled with 'Unknown' for TerritoryName and TerritoryGroup rather than dropped
They are automatically deleted by pd.merge
They cause pd.merge to throw an error
They are duplicated instead of merged
questions.explain: fillna("Unknown") labels unmatched rows clearly instead of losing them from the totals.

questions.q: What sanity check confirms the left join went correctly?
options: combined_df's row count should equal customer_df's row count exactly
combined_df should have zero columns
combined_df should have more rows than customer_df times two
combined_df should always equal territory_df's row count
questions.explain: A left join only adds columns, never adds or removes rows from the left side, when the join key is as unique as assumed.
